note: Items for the English-only L1 lessons and the compliance objective. English-only by design: these belong to lessons that ship English-only in this build, and a learner should not meet an Arabic question inside an English lesson. The flagship lesson's items (MI-05, MI-06) are bilingual and live in their own file. No knowledge checks here: these lessons ship at L1, where knowledge_check blocks are not allowed, so a formative item would be unreachable.

items.stemAr: Which party carries the financial risk?
items.stemEn: Which party carries the financial risk?
items.rationaleAr: The payer carries the risk and sets the rules a claim is judged against. A TPA may process claims without carrying either.
items.rationaleEn: The payer carries the risk and sets the rules a claim is judged against. A TPA may process claims without carrying either.

options.textAr: The payer
options.textEn: The payer
options.feedbackAr: Correct. Carrying the risk is what makes it the payer rather than an administrator.
options.feedbackEn: Correct. Carrying the risk is what makes it the payer rather than an administrator.

options.textAr: The third-party administrator
options.textEn: The third-party administrator
options.feedbackAr: A TPA processes claims on the payer's behalf without carrying the risk; the rules are still the payer's.
options.feedbackEn: A TPA processes claims on the payer's behalf without carrying the risk; the rules are still the payer's.

options.textAr: The provider
options.textEn: The provider
options.feedbackAr: The provider carries the risk of not being paid, which is a different thing from insuring the member.
options.feedbackEn: The provider carries the risk of not being paid, which is a different thing from insuring the member.

options.textAr: The member
options.textEn: The member
options.feedbackAr: The member bears cost sharing, but the insured risk sits with the payer.
options.feedbackEn: The member bears cost sharing, but the insured risk sits with the payer.

items.stemAr: A premium is paid at which point relative to care?
items.stemEn: A premium is paid at which point relative to care?
items.rationaleAr: Premiums are paid before any care, which is what makes insurance a pooled arrangement rather than a payment plan.
items.rationaleEn: Premiums are paid before any care, which is what makes insurance a pooled arrangement rather than a payment plan.

options.textAr: Before care, whether or not any is needed
options.textEn: Before care, whether or not any is needed
options.feedbackAr: Correct. That is what pooling means: payment precedes and is independent of use.
options.feedbackEn: Correct. That is what pooling means: payment precedes and is independent of use.

options.textAr: After care, once the claim is adjudicated
options.textEn: After care, once the claim is adjudicated
options.feedbackAr: That describes the payer paying the provider, not the member paying the premium.
options.feedbackEn: That describes the payer paying the provider, not the member paying the premium.

options.textAr: At the time of the visit
options.textEn: At the time of the visit
options.feedbackAr: A payment at the visit is cost sharing or self-pay, not a premium.
options.feedbackEn: A payment at the visit is cost sharing or self-pay, not a premium.

options.textAr: Only when a claim is denied
options.textEn: Only when a claim is denied
options.feedbackAr: Denial changes who owes the balance; it does not trigger a premium.
options.feedbackEn: Denial changes who owes the balance; it does not trigger a premium.

items.stemAr: A patient is told "the TPA denied it". Who set the rule that produced the denial?
items.stemEn: A patient is told "the TPA denied it". Who set the rule that produced the denial?
items.rationaleAr: A TPA applies the payer's rules. Tracing a decision to the rule-setter is what makes it possible to challenge.
items.rationaleEn: A TPA applies the payer's rules. Tracing a decision to the rule-setter is what makes it possible to challenge.

options.textAr: The payer
options.textEn: The payer
options.feedbackAr: Correct. The administrator applied someone else's rule, and that is who the challenge is really with.
options.feedbackEn: Correct. The administrator applied someone else's rule, and that is who the challenge is really with.

options.textAr: The TPA
options.textEn: The TPA
options.feedbackAr: The TPA applied the rule; it did not write it. This confusion sends appeals to the wrong place.
options.feedbackEn: The TPA applied the rule; it did not write it. This confusion sends appeals to the wrong place.

options.textAr: The provider
options.textEn: The provider
options.feedbackAr: The provider submitted the claim and does not set coverage rules.
options.feedbackEn: The provider submitted the claim and does not set coverage rules.

options.textAr: The clearinghouse
options.textEn: The clearinghouse
options.feedbackAr: A clearinghouse checks format and routes claims; it makes no coverage decisions.
options.feedbackEn: A clearinghouse checks format and routes claims; it makes no coverage decisions.

items.stemAr: Which of these move money? Select all that apply.
items.stemEn: Which of these move money? Select all that apply.
items.rationaleAr: Premium and payment move money. Care is a service, and a claim is a request rather than a transfer.
items.rationaleEn: Premium and payment move money. Care is a service, and a claim is a request rather than a transfer.

options.textAr: The premium
options.textEn: The premium
options.feedbackAr: Correct — money, before any care.
options.feedbackEn: Correct — money, before any care.

options.textAr: The payer's payment to the provider
options.textEn: The payer's payment to the provider
options.feedbackAr: Correct — money, after adjudication.
options.feedbackEn: Correct — money, after adjudication.

options.textAr: The claim
options.textEn: The claim
options.feedbackAr: A claim is a request for payment, not a payment. Treating it as money is why "submitted" gets confused with "paid".
options.feedbackEn: A claim is a request for payment, not a payment. Treating it as money is why "submitted" gets confused with "paid".

options.textAr: The delivery of care
options.textEn: The delivery of care
options.feedbackAr: Care is the service being paid for, moving in the opposite direction to money.
options.feedbackEn: Care is the service being paid for, moving in the opposite direction to money.

items.stemAr: Why does most administrative difficulty in this field trace back to one structural fact?
items.stemEn: Why does most administrative difficulty in this field trace back to one structural fact?
items.rationaleAr: The person receiving the service is usually not the person paying, so every service needs a documented justification addressed to a third party.
items.rationaleEn: The person receiving the service is usually not the person paying, so every service needs a documented justification addressed to a third party.

options.textAr: The recipient of care is not the payer, so every service must be justified to a third party
options.textEn: The recipient of care is not the payer, so every service must be justified to a third party
options.feedbackAr: Correct. Nearly every rule in the field exists to bridge that gap.
options.feedbackEn: Correct. Nearly every rule in the field exists to bridge that gap.

options.textAr: Medical services are inherently expensive
options.textEn: Medical services are inherently expensive
options.feedbackAr: Cost explains why insurance exists, not why the paperwork works this way.
options.feedbackEn: Cost explains why insurance exists, not why the paperwork works this way.

options.textAr: Providers and payers use different software
options.textEn: Providers and payers use different software
options.feedbackAr: A real friction, but a symptom rather than the structural cause.
options.feedbackEn: A real friction, but a symptom rather than the structural cause.

options.textAr: Regulations change frequently
options.textEn: Regulations change frequently
options.feedbackAr: Change adds work; the separation of recipient and payer creates the work in the first place.
options.feedbackEn: Change adds work; the separation of recipient and payer creates the work in the first place.

items.stemAr: Active coverage on the service date means the service will be paid.
items.stemEn: Active coverage on the service date means the service will be paid.
items.rationaleAr: Active coverage is necessary but not sufficient: the service must also be covered, and may require pre-authorisation.
items.rationaleEn: Active coverage is necessary but not sufficient: the service must also be covered, and may require pre-authorisation.

options.textAr: False — coverage may be active and the service still unpayable
options.textEn: False — coverage may be active and the service still unpayable
options.feedbackAr: Correct. Eligibility and permission are separate questions.
options.feedbackEn: Correct. Eligibility and permission are separate questions.

options.textAr: True — active coverage is what payment depends on
options.textEn: True — active coverage is what payment depends on
options.feedbackAr: This is the single most common eligibility error: treating active coverage as permission.
options.feedbackEn: This is the single most common eligibility error: treating active coverage as permission.

items.stemAr: Coverage is active, and the payer requires pre-authorisation for the planned service, which has not been obtained. What is the correct action?
items.stemEn: Coverage is active, and the payer requires pre-authorisation for the planned service, which has not been obtained. What is the correct action?
items.rationaleAr: Pre-authorisation usually cannot be obtained retroactively, so the decision must be made before delivery.
items.rationaleEn: Pre-authorisation usually cannot be obtained retroactively, so the decision must be made before delivery.

options.textAr: Obtain pre-authorisation before delivering the service
options.textEn: Obtain pre-authorisation before delivering the service
options.feedbackAr: Correct. Afterwards the option is usually gone, whatever the clinical merit.
options.feedbackEn: Correct. Afterwards the option is usually gone, whatever the clinical merit.

options.textAr: Deliver the service and request authorisation afterwards
options.textEn: Deliver the service and request authorisation afterwards
options.feedbackAr: Retroactive authorisation is rarely available; this converts a solvable problem into an unpayable claim.
options.feedbackEn: Retroactive authorisation is rarely available; this converts a solvable problem into an unpayable claim.

options.textAr: Deliver and submit, since coverage is active
options.textEn: Deliver and submit, since coverage is active
options.feedbackAr: Active coverage is not permission. This is the error the lesson is built around.
options.feedbackEn: Active coverage is not permission. This is the error the lesson is built around.

options.textAr: Convert to self-pay immediately
options.textEn: Convert to self-pay immediately
options.feedbackAr: Premature: authorisation may well be granted, and the member loses a benefit they hold.
options.feedbackEn: Premature: authorisation may well be granted, and the member loses a benefit they hold.

items.stemAr: What does an eligibility check ask?
items.stemEn: What does an eligibility check ask?
items.rationaleAr: It asks whether active coverage exists for this member, on this date, for this category of service.
items.rationaleEn: It asks whether active coverage exists for this member, on this date, for this category of service.

options.textAr: Whether coverage is active for this member on this date
options.textEn: Whether coverage is active for this member on this date
options.feedbackAr: Correct. It is a question about the policy, not the patient's condition.
options.feedbackEn: Correct. It is a question about the policy, not the patient's condition.

options.textAr: Whether the service is medically appropriate
options.textEn: Whether the service is medically appropriate
options.feedbackAr: That is medical necessity, judged from the record after the fact.
options.feedbackEn: That is medical necessity, judged from the record after the fact.

options.textAr: Whether the provider is accepting new patients
options.textEn: Whether the provider is accepting new patients
options.feedbackAr: An operational question unrelated to coverage.
options.feedbackEn: An operational question unrelated to coverage.

options.textAr: Whether the claim was formatted correctly
options.textEn: Whether the claim was formatted correctly
options.feedbackAr: That is checked at submission, long after eligibility.
options.feedbackEn: That is checked at submission, long after eligibility.

items.stemAr: Which are legitimate outcomes of an eligibility check? Select all that apply.
items.stemEn: Which are legitimate outcomes of an eligibility check? Select all that apply.
items.rationaleAr: Proceed, pre-authorise first, or convert to self-pay. Adjusting a date is falsification, not an outcome.
items.rationaleEn: Proceed, pre-authorise first, or convert to self-pay. Adjusting a date is falsification, not an outcome.

options.textAr: Proceed with the service
options.textEn: Proceed with the service
options.feedbackAr: Correct — coverage active and no permission required.
options.feedbackEn: Correct — coverage active and no permission required.

options.textAr: Obtain pre-authorisation first
options.textEn: Obtain pre-authorisation first
options.feedbackAr: Correct — coverage active but permission required.
options.feedbackEn: Correct — coverage active but permission required.

options.textAr: Change the service date so it falls inside the coverage period
options.textEn: Change the service date so it falls inside the coverage period
options.feedbackAr: Not an outcome — a falsification. The date of service is a fact.
options.feedbackEn: Not an outcome — a falsification. The date of service is a fact.

options.textAr: Submit anyway and see what happens
options.textEn: Submit anyway and see what happens
options.feedbackAr: Not a decision. It spends a cycle to learn what the check already told you.
options.feedbackEn: Not a decision. It spends a cycle to learn what the check already told you.

items.stemAr: Why record the reference number from an eligibility response?
items.stemEn: Why record the reference number from an eligibility response?
items.rationaleAr: Without it a later dispute is recollection against record, which is not a dispute the provider wins.
items.rationaleEn: Without it a later dispute is recollection against record, which is not a dispute the provider wins.

options.textAr: It makes a later dispute winnable rather than a matter of recollection
options.textEn: It makes a later dispute winnable rather than a matter of recollection
options.feedbackAr: Correct. The reference is the evidence that the answer was given.
options.feedbackEn: Correct. The reference is the evidence that the answer was given.

options.textAr: It speeds up claim processing
options.textEn: It speeds up claim processing
options.feedbackAr: It does not affect processing speed; it matters only in dispute.
options.feedbackEn: It does not affect processing speed; it matters only in dispute.

options.textAr: It is required on the claim form
options.textEn: It is required on the claim form
options.feedbackAr: Not a claim field; it is a record of the conversation.
options.feedbackEn: Not a claim field; it is a record of the conversation.

options.textAr: It proves the service was medically necessary
options.textEn: It proves the service was medically necessary
options.feedbackAr: Eligibility says nothing about necessity, which is judged from the clinical record.
options.feedbackEn: Eligibility says nothing about necessity, which is judged from the clinical record.

items.stemAr: A claim is returned before the payer assesses it. Rejection or denial?
items.stemEn: A claim is returned before the payer assesses it. Rejection or denial?
items.rationaleAr: A rejection stops the claim before assessment; a denial follows assessment.
items.rationaleEn: A rejection stops the claim before assessment; a denial follows assessment.

options.textAr: Rejection
options.textEn: Rejection
options.feedbackAr: Correct. Nothing was judged — the claim never entered assessment.
options.feedbackEn: Correct. Nothing was judged — the claim never entered assessment.

options.textAr: Denial
options.textEn: Denial
options.feedbackAr: A denial means it was read and refused. Here it was never read.
options.feedbackEn: A denial means it was read and refused. Here it was never read.

items.stemAr: Why does the rejection/denial distinction change what you do next?
items.stemEn: Why does the rejection/denial distinction change what you do next?
items.rationaleAr: A rejection is corrected and resubmitted as a new claim; a denial is a decision, addressed by correction or appeal.
items.rationaleEn: A rejection is corrected and resubmitted as a new claim; a denial is a decision, addressed by correction or appeal.

options.textAr: A rejection is corrected and resubmitted; a denial is a decision to be corrected or appealed
options.textEn: A rejection is corrected and resubmitted; a denial is a decision to be corrected or appealed
options.feedbackAr: Correct. The distinction picks the route, which is why the words are not interchangeable.
options.feedbackEn: Correct. The distinction picks the route, which is why the words are not interchangeable.

options.textAr: A rejection is more serious than a denial
options.textEn: A rejection is more serious than a denial
options.feedbackAr: Usually the reverse: a rejection is often a data fix, while a denial has been judged.
options.feedbackEn: Usually the reverse: a rejection is often a data fix, while a denial has been judged.

options.textAr: Only denials can be appealed, so rejections are final
options.textEn: Only denials can be appealed, so rejections are final
options.feedbackAr: Rejections are not final at all — they are corrected and resubmitted.
options.feedbackEn: Rejections are not final at all — they are corrected and resubmitted.

options.textAr: They differ only in the wording of the notice
options.textEn: They differ only in the wording of the notice
options.feedbackAr: They differ in whether assessment happened, which changes the remedy.
options.feedbackEn: They differ in whether assessment happened, which changes the remedy.

items.stemAr: A claim is refused because the service preceded the policy effective date. How is it classified?
items.stemEn: A claim is refused because the service preceded the policy effective date. How is it classified?
items.rationaleAr: It was assessed and refused on coverage grounds, which makes it a denial with an eligibility root cause.
items.rationaleEn: It was assessed and refused on coverage grounds, which makes it a denial with an eligibility root cause.

options.textAr: A denial, root cause eligibility
options.textEn: A denial, root cause eligibility
options.feedbackAr: Correct. It was read and judged against the policy period.
options.feedbackEn: Correct. It was read and judged against the policy period.

options.textAr: A rejection, because the data was wrong
options.textEn: A rejection, because the data was wrong
options.feedbackAr: The data was correct; the coverage was not in force. Nothing here is a formatting failure.
options.feedbackEn: The data was correct; the coverage was not in force. Nothing here is a formatting failure.

options.textAr: A denial, root cause documentation
options.textEn: A denial, root cause documentation
options.feedbackAr: Documentation concerns whether the record supports the service, which is not the issue.
options.feedbackEn: Documentation concerns whether the record supports the service, which is not the issue.

options.textAr: A duplicate
options.textEn: A duplicate
options.feedbackAr: Nothing suggests the service was claimed twice.
options.feedbackEn: Nothing suggests the service was claimed twice.

items.stemAr: Which of these produce a rejection rather than a denial? Select all that apply.
items.stemEn: Which of these produce a rejection rather than a denial? Select all that apply.
items.rationaleAr: Format and identity failures stop a claim before assessment; coverage and documentation judgements come after it.
items.rationaleEn: Format and identity failures stop a claim before assessment; coverage and documentation judgements come after it.

options.textAr: A date written in an unaccepted format
options.textEn: A date written in an unaccepted format
options.feedbackAr: Correct — the claim cannot be read, so it is not assessed.
options.feedbackEn: Correct — the claim cannot be read, so it is not assessed.

options.textAr: A member identifier that does not match the payer's record
options.textEn: A member identifier that does not match the payer's record
options.feedbackAr: Correct — the claim cannot be matched to a policy, so assessment never starts.
options.feedbackEn: Correct — the claim cannot be matched to a policy, so assessment never starts.

options.textAr: A service excluded by the policy
options.textEn: A service excluded by the policy
options.feedbackAr: That requires reading the claim and the policy: a denial.
options.feedbackEn: That requires reading the claim and the policy: a denial.

options.textAr: A record that does not support the level billed
options.textEn: A record that does not support the level billed
options.feedbackAr: A judgement about evidence, made after assessment.
options.feedbackEn: A judgement about evidence, made after assessment.

items.stemAr: A denial states the record does not support the level billed, and on review it does not. What is the correct action?
items.stemEn: A denial states the record does not support the level billed, and on review it does not. What is the correct action?
items.rationaleAr: Correct the claim to match the record. Changing the record to match the claim is falsification.
items.rationaleEn: Correct the claim to match the record. Changing the record to match the claim is falsification.

options.textAr: Correct the claim to match the record and resubmit
options.textEn: Correct the claim to match the record and resubmit
options.feedbackAr: Correct. The record is the evidence; the claim is the assertion, and the assertion is what changes.
options.feedbackEn: Correct. The record is the evidence; the claim is the assertion, and the assertion is what changes.

options.textAr: Appeal, citing the clinician's judgement
options.textEn: Appeal, citing the clinician's judgement
options.feedbackAr: An appeal without new evidence loses and consumes the filing window.
options.feedbackEn: An appeal without new evidence loses and consumes the filing window.

options.textAr: Amend the record to describe what was billed
options.textEn: Amend the record to describe what was billed
options.feedbackAr: That is falsification, and it turns a billing error into an integrity matter.
options.feedbackEn: That is falsification, and it turns a billing error into an integrity matter.

options.textAr: Write the claim off immediately
options.textEn: Write the claim off immediately
options.feedbackAr: Premature: a corrected claim for the supported level is usually payable.
options.feedbackEn: Premature: a corrected claim for the supported level is usually payable.

items.stemAr: What is the most expensive common mistake in denial work?
items.stemEn: What is the most expensive common mistake in denial work?
items.rationaleAr: Appealing what should have been corrected: appeals are slow, consume the filing window, and lose when the cause was a data error.
items.rationaleEn: Appealing what should have been corrected: appeals are slow, consume the filing window, and lose when the cause was a data error.

options.textAr: Appealing something that should have been corrected and resubmitted
options.textEn: Appealing something that should have been corrected and resubmitted
options.feedbackAr: Correct. It spends the slowest remedy on the cheapest problem.
options.feedbackEn: Correct. It spends the slowest remedy on the cheapest problem.

options.textAr: Correcting something that should have been appealed
options.textEn: Correcting something that should have been appealed
options.feedbackAr: A real error, but a corrected resubmission usually still lands inside the window.
options.feedbackEn: A real error, but a corrected resubmission usually still lands inside the window.

options.textAr: Writing off small balances
options.textEn: Writing off small balances
options.feedbackAr: A commercial judgement, not a classification error.
options.feedbackEn: A commercial judgement, not a classification error.

options.textAr: Resubmitting too quickly
options.textEn: Resubmitting too quickly
options.feedbackAr: Speed is rarely the problem; misclassification is.
options.feedbackEn: Speed is rarely the problem; misclassification is.

items.stemAr: A denial cites timely filing. Which responses are defensible? Select all that apply.
items.stemEn: A denial cites timely filing. Which responses are defensible? Select all that apply.
items.rationaleAr: Only evidence of timely submission supports an appeal. Resubmitting or backdating does not.
items.rationaleEn: Only evidence of timely submission supports an appeal. Resubmitting or backdating does not.

options.textAr: Appeal with evidence the claim was submitted inside the window
options.textEn: Appeal with evidence the claim was submitted inside the window
options.feedbackAr: Correct — the appeal turns on proof of submission date.
options.feedbackEn: Correct — the appeal turns on proof of submission date.

options.textAr: Accept the denial where no such evidence exists
options.textEn: Accept the denial where no such evidence exists
options.feedbackAr: Correct. Accepting a correct denial is a legitimate outcome, not a failure.
options.feedbackEn: Correct. Accepting a correct denial is a legitimate outcome, not a failure.

options.textAr: Resubmit the claim unchanged
options.textEn: Resubmit the claim unchanged
options.feedbackAr: The deadline has already passed; resubmission cannot cure lateness.
options.feedbackEn: The deadline has already passed; resubmission cannot cure lateness.

options.textAr: Change the submission date on the claim
options.textEn: Change the submission date on the claim
options.feedbackAr: Falsification, and easily disproved by the payer's own receipt records.
options.feedbackEn: Falsification, and easily disproved by the payer's own receipt records.

items.stemAr: A denial is for a duplicate claim, and the service genuinely was claimed before. What is the correct action?
items.stemEn: A denial is for a duplicate claim, and the service genuinely was claimed before. What is the correct action?
items.rationaleAr: Withdraw. Resubmitting a genuine duplicate creates a second problem rather than solving the first.
items.rationaleEn: Withdraw. Resubmitting a genuine duplicate creates a second problem rather than solving the first.

options.textAr: Withdraw the claim and do not resubmit
options.textEn: Withdraw the claim and do not resubmit
options.feedbackAr: Correct. The original claim is the one to follow up.
options.feedbackEn: Correct. The original claim is the one to follow up.

options.textAr: Resubmit with a note explaining it is not a duplicate
options.textEn: Resubmit with a note explaining it is not a duplicate
options.feedbackAr: It is a duplicate. A note asserting otherwise is inaccurate.
options.feedbackEn: It is a duplicate. A note asserting otherwise is inaccurate.

options.textAr: Appeal the duplicate determination
options.textEn: Appeal the duplicate determination
options.feedbackAr: There is nothing to appeal: the determination is correct.
options.feedbackEn: There is nothing to appeal: the determination is correct.

options.textAr: Bill the patient for the difference
options.textEn: Bill the patient for the difference
options.feedbackAr: The service was already claimed; billing the patient for it compounds the error.
options.feedbackEn: The service was already claimed; billing the patient for it compounds the error.

items.stemAr: A colleague suggests coding an extended assessment because "that level is always used for this visit type", though the record describes a brief review. What is this?
items.stemEn: A colleague suggests coding an extended assessment because "that level is always used for this visit type", though the record describes a brief review. What is this?
items.rationaleAr: Billing a level above what the record supports is upcoding, whatever the local custom.
items.rationaleEn: Billing a level above what the record supports is upcoding, whatever the local custom.

options.textAr: Upcoding — billing above what the record supports
options.textEn: Upcoding — billing above what the record supports
options.feedbackAr: Correct. Custom is not evidence, and the record is what a reviewer reads.
options.feedbackEn: Correct. Custom is not evidence, and the record is what a reviewer reads.

options.textAr: A reasonable interpretation of an ambiguous record
options.textEn: A reasonable interpretation of an ambiguous record
options.feedbackAr: The record is not ambiguous here; it describes a brief review. This is the rationalisation the callout warns about.
options.feedbackEn: The record is not ambiguous here; it describes a brief review. This is the rationalisation the callout warns about.

options.textAr: Unbundling
options.textEn: Unbundling
options.feedbackAr: Unbundling splits one service into parts; this inflates the level of a single service.
options.feedbackEn: Unbundling splits one service into parts; this inflates the level of a single service.

options.textAr: A documentation gap, to be fixed by the clinician
options.textEn: A documentation gap, to be fixed by the clinician
options.feedbackAr: The record is not missing anything — it simply does not support the higher level.
options.feedbackEn: The record is not missing anything — it simply does not support the higher level.

items.stemAr: One procedure is submitted as three separate lines, each paid individually, where the payer expects a single combined line. What is this called?
items.stemEn: One procedure is submitted as three separate lines, each paid individually, where the payer expects a single combined line. What is this called?
items.rationaleAr: Splitting one service into separately paid parts is unbundling.
items.rationaleEn: Splitting one service into separately paid parts is unbundling.

options.textAr: Unbundling
options.textEn: Unbundling
options.feedbackAr: Correct. The parts are real; presenting them separately to be paid more is the problem.
options.feedbackEn: Correct. The parts are real; presenting them separately to be paid more is the problem.

options.textAr: Upcoding
options.textEn: Upcoding
options.feedbackAr: Upcoding raises the level of one service rather than splitting it into several.
options.feedbackEn: Upcoding raises the level of one service rather than splitting it into several.

options.textAr: A duplicate claim
options.textEn: A duplicate claim
options.feedbackAr: A duplicate re-bills the same thing; here the service is described differently.
options.feedbackEn: A duplicate re-bills the same thing; here the service is described differently.

options.textAr: A timely filing issue
options.textEn: A timely filing issue
options.feedbackAr: Nothing here concerns when the claim was submitted.
options.feedbackEn: Nothing here concerns when the claim was submitted.

items.stemAr: A "correction" increases the amount owed, and nothing in the record changed. What should you do?
items.stemEn: A "correction" increases the amount owed, and nothing in the record changed. What should you do?
items.rationaleAr: A change in payment with no change in evidence is the signal to stop and ask what is actually being corrected.
items.rationaleEn: A change in payment with no change in evidence is the signal to stop and ask what is actually being corrected.

options.textAr: Stop and establish what evidence supports the increase
options.textEn: Stop and establish what evidence supports the increase
options.feedbackAr: Correct. Payment changing while evidence does not is the warning sign the callout names.
options.feedbackEn: Correct. Payment changing while evidence does not is the warning sign the callout names.

options.textAr: Submit it, since corrections are routine
options.textEn: Submit it, since corrections are routine
options.feedbackAr: Routine is exactly how this passes unnoticed. The system did not stop it, so a person is answerable.
options.feedbackEn: Routine is exactly how this passes unnoticed. The system did not stop it, so a person is answerable.

options.textAr: Submit it and flag it for audit later
options.textEn: Submit it and flag it for audit later
options.feedbackAr: Submitting a claim you cannot yet justify is the action under question; flagging afterwards does not undo it.
options.feedbackEn: Submitting a claim you cannot yet justify is the action under question; flagging afterwards does not undo it.

options.textAr: Reduce the amount instead
options.textEn: Reduce the amount instead
options.feedbackAr: Under-billing is also inaccurate. The aim is a claim the record supports, not a lower number.
options.feedbackEn: Under-billing is also inaccurate. The aim is a claim the record supports, not a lower number.

items.stemAr: Why are upcoding and unbundling treated as integrity matters rather than data errors? Select all that apply.
items.stemEn: Why are upcoding and unbundling treated as integrity matters rather than data errors? Select all that apply.
items.rationaleAr: Both often pass automated edits, and both increase payment without any change in what was delivered.
items.rationaleEn: Both often pass automated edits, and both increase payment without any change in what was delivered.

options.textAr: They frequently pass automated checks, so no system catches them
options.textEn: They frequently pass automated checks, so no system catches them
options.feedbackAr: Correct — which is why a person is answerable for them.
options.feedbackEn: Correct — which is why a person is answerable for them.

options.textAr: They increase payment without any change in what was delivered
options.textEn: They increase payment without any change in what was delivered
options.feedbackAr: Correct. Payment moves while the underlying facts do not.
options.feedbackEn: Correct. Payment moves while the underlying facts do not.

options.textAr: They are always the result of deliberate fraud
options.textEn: They are always the result of deliberate fraud
options.feedbackAr: Often they are drift or pressure rather than intent, which is why the rule is about evidence and not motive.
options.feedbackEn: Often they are drift or pressure rather than intent, which is why the rule is about evidence and not motive.

options.textAr: They can only occur in electronic claims
options.textEn: They can only occur in electronic claims
options.feedbackAr: The medium is irrelevant to either.
options.feedbackEn: The medium is irrelevant to either.

items.stemAr: The record reads "imaging to be arranged". Imaging is billed. Is the line supported?
items.stemEn: The record reads "imaging to be arranged". Imaging is billed. Is the line supported?
items.rationaleAr: An intention is not evidence that a service happened. Support requires the record to show it was performed.
items.rationaleEn: An intention is not evidence that a service happened. Support requires the record to show it was performed.

options.textAr: No — the record states an intention, not a performed service
options.textEn: No — the record states an intention, not a performed service
options.feedbackAr: Correct. "To be arranged" describes a plan; a reviewer needs evidence it took place.
options.feedbackEn: Correct. "To be arranged" describes a plan; a reviewer needs evidence it took place.

options.textAr: Yes — arranging imaging implies it was done
options.textEn: Yes — arranging imaging implies it was done
options.feedbackAr: Implication is not evidence. This is precisely the inference a reviewer will refuse to make.
options.feedbackEn: Implication is not evidence. This is precisely the inference a reviewer will refuse to make.

options.textAr: Yes, provided the clinician confirms it verbally
options.textEn: Yes, provided the clinician confirms it verbally
options.feedbackAr: A later verbal confirmation is not what was documented at the time of service.
options.feedbackEn: A later verbal confirmation is not what was documented at the time of service.

options.textAr: Only if the payer requires no pre-authorisation
options.textEn: Only if the payer requires no pre-authorisation
options.feedbackAr: Authorisation is a separate question; the line is unsupported either way.
options.feedbackEn: Authorisation is a separate question; the line is unsupported either way.

items.stemAr: Which statements in a record support billing an extended assessment? Select all that apply.
items.stemEn: Which statements in a record support billing an extended assessment? Select all that apply.
items.rationaleAr: Support needs the service to be described as performed, with enough detail to distinguish it from a lesser one.
items.rationaleEn: Support needs the service to be described as performed, with enough detail to distinguish it from a lesser one.

options.textAr: "Extended assessment performed; findings recorded."
options.textEn: "Extended assessment performed; findings recorded."
options.feedbackAr: Correct — performed, and described at the level billed.
options.feedbackEn: Correct — performed, and described at the level billed.

options.textAr: "Full history and examination completed, findings documented below."
options.textEn: "Full history and examination completed, findings documented below."
options.feedbackAr: Correct — describes work consistent with the level billed.
options.feedbackEn: Correct — describes work consistent with the level billed.

options.textAr: "Patient reviewed."
options.textEn: "Patient reviewed."
options.feedbackAr: Describes something happening, but not at the level billed. This is where upcoding starts.
options.feedbackEn: Describes something happening, but not at the level billed. This is where upcoding starts.

options.textAr: "Extended assessment scheduled for next week."
options.textEn: "Extended assessment scheduled for next week."
options.feedbackAr: A future service cannot support a current claim.
options.feedbackEn: A future service cannot support a current claim.

items.stemAr: A claim is returned by the clearinghouse before reaching the payer. What is the correct term and next step?
items.stemEn: A claim is returned by the clearinghouse before reaching the payer. What is the correct term and next step?
items.rationaleAr: Nothing was assessed, so it is a rejection: correct the data or format and resubmit.
items.rationaleEn: Nothing was assessed, so it is a rejection: correct the data or format and resubmit.

options.textAr: A rejection — correct and resubmit
options.textEn: A rejection — correct and resubmit
options.feedbackAr: Correct. No decision was made, so there is nothing to appeal.
options.feedbackEn: Correct. No decision was made, so there is nothing to appeal.

options.textAr: A denial — file an appeal
options.textEn: A denial — file an appeal
options.feedbackAr: An appeal argues against a decision, and no decision exists yet.
options.feedbackEn: An appeal argues against a decision, and no decision exists yet.

options.textAr: A denial — bill the patient
options.textEn: A denial — bill the patient
options.feedbackAr: The payer has not refused anything; billing the patient here is premature and probably wrong.
options.feedbackEn: The payer has not refused anything; billing the patient here is premature and probably wrong.

options.textAr: A duplicate — withdraw the claim
options.textEn: A duplicate — withdraw the claim
options.feedbackAr: Nothing indicates the service was claimed twice.
options.feedbackEn: Nothing indicates the service was claimed twice.

items.stemAr: Which single question most reliably decides how to respond to a denial?
items.stemEn: Which single question most reliably decides how to respond to a denial?
items.rationaleAr: The root cause decides the action. The notice wording often describes the symptom rather than the cause.
items.rationaleEn: The root cause decides the action. The notice wording often describes the symptom rather than the cause.

options.textAr: What was the root cause?
options.textEn: What was the root cause?
options.feedbackAr: Correct. Cause picks the route; everything else follows from it.
options.feedbackEn: Correct. Cause picks the route; everything else follows from it.

options.textAr: How much money is at stake?
options.textEn: How much money is at stake?
options.feedbackAr: Relevant to whether to pursue it, not to which action is correct.
options.feedbackEn: Relevant to whether to pursue it, not to which action is correct.

options.textAr: Which payer issued it?
options.textEn: Which payer issued it?
options.feedbackAr: Useful context, but the same cause takes the same route across payers.
options.feedbackEn: Useful context, but the same cause takes the same route across payers.

options.textAr: What does the denial notice say?
options.textEn: What does the denial notice say?
options.feedbackAr: The notice is evidence about the cause, not the cause itself — and often describes the symptom.
options.feedbackEn: The notice is evidence about the cause, not the cause itself — and often describes the symptom.

items.stemAr: Which is the strongest single defence when asked to bill something the record does not show?
items.stemEn: Which is the strongest single defence when asked to bill something the record does not show?
items.rationaleAr: Pointing at the record moves the conversation from opinion to evidence, and is the same defence in an audit.
items.rationaleEn: Pointing at the record moves the conversation from opinion to evidence, and is the same defence in an audit.

options.textAr: Point at the record and ask what evidence supports the change
options.textEn: Point at the record and ask what evidence supports the change
options.feedbackAr: Correct. It is the same question an auditor asks, and asking it early is cheaper.
options.feedbackEn: Correct. It is the same question an auditor asks, and asking it early is cheaper.

options.textAr: Defer to the more senior colleague
options.textEn: Defer to the more senior colleague
options.feedbackAr: Seniority is not evidence, and it does not transfer answerability for the claim.
options.feedbackEn: Seniority is not evidence, and it does not transfer answerability for the claim.

options.textAr: Submit it and note your disagreement internally
options.textEn: Submit it and note your disagreement internally
options.feedbackAr: The claim still goes out asserting something unsupported; a private note does not change that.
options.feedbackEn: The claim still goes out asserting something unsupported; a private note does not change that.

options.textAr: Ask the payer whether it would be accepted
options.textEn: Ask the payer whether it would be accepted
options.feedbackAr: Acceptance is not the test. A claim can be paid and still be unsupported.
options.feedbackEn: Acceptance is not the test. A claim can be paid and still be unsupported.
